newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ANALYSIS-RESULTS, EU NEWS KEEP ESTONIA MARKET BUBBLING.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS-RESULTS, EU NEWS KEEP ESTONIA MARKET BUBBLING.

text.p: Strong half year results, supported by news that Estonia is to be included in the first wave of EU expansion talks, has kept the Estonian bourse on the boil and beating new records, analysts said on Friday.
Dealers said the long-term upward trend was set to continue although some profit-taking was possible.
The bourse index has risen 6.8 percent over four days, hitting a new record level of 322.86 on Thursday.
The rise was mostly backed by leading banking shares Hansapank , which gained 8.6 percent, and Hoiupank, higher by 8.9 percent.
"The upward momentum is based on solid half-year results and expectations for higher profit forecasts," an analyst said.
The banks' half-year results were substantially better than previous estimates. Hansapank and Uhispank have already officially said they will raise their 1997 forecasts.
Analysts said that the news on Estonia's EU invite has also sparked interest from foreign investors.
"Many foreign investors have become interested...they want to get something in Estonian assets," one dealer said.
The U.S. dollar, strengthening further during the week, has also benefited shares in drug company Farmaatsiatehas and diversfied industrialist Norma, analysts said.
"Farmaatsiatehas and Norma earn more profit from a favourable dollar exchange rate," one dealer said, adding they have more potential to gain.
Norma's gain of 5.8 percent during the week was also affected by a deal of 121 million kroons, when its parent company sold 11.9 percent to Western investors.
"It confirmed the confidence in local shares," one trader said.
